scenario.name: DNS Tunneling C2 & High-Entropy Subdomain Data Exfiltration
scenario.shortSubtitle: Network & Log Analysis · Bypassing Egress Firewall via Recursive DNS
scenario.overview: Think of a classic neighborhood post office with brass P.O. boxes lining the back wall, a parcel scale counter, a blue street mailbox outside, and angled mail sorting chutes. At the neighborhood post office counter, a sender slips tiny coded lines onto the back of ordinary postcards and drops them one by one into the mail sorting slot. In this real-world scenario, the intruder steps up to the postal scale & stamp window blending in with everyday guests, then smuggles copied records out past the postal scale & stamp window in tiny disguised batches. The postmaster reviews the evening dispatch ledger and spots hundreds of oddly coded postcards all mailed to the exact same remote P.O. box. In this scenario (T1071.004, DNS Tunneling C2 & High-Entropy Subdomain Data Exfiltration) at 10.50.1, the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: chunking (PID 4412, running as CORP\svc_backup), then recursive Relay Through the Corporate DNS (ns1.badactor-dns.net at 45.133.1.99:53), then reassembling Exfiltrated CSV Chunks (ns1.badactor-dns.net, 45.133.1.99:53). Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering Chunking (PID 4412, running as CORP\svc_backup), then Recursive Relay Through the Corporate DNS (ns1.badactor-dns.net at 45.133.1.99:53), then Reassembling Exfiltrated CSV Chunks (ns1.badactor-dns.net, 45.133.1.99:53). Primary detection correlates Sysmon Event 22 with the documented host and network chain.

stages.title: CHUNK & HEX-ENCODE STOLEN DATA INTO SUBDOMAINS
stages.subtitle: Sysmon Event ID 22 captures high-entropy DNS query from sync_agent.exe
stages.description: At the neighborhood post office counter, a sender slips tiny coded lines onto the back of ordinary postcards and drops them one by one into the mail sorting slot. Specifically in Step 1, the intruder steps up to the postal scale & stamp window blending in with everyday guests while everyday visitors and the postal clerk go about their routine. On the isolated database host DB-BACKUP-02 (10.50.1.12, which has no direct internet access because the Egress Firewall blocks TCP ports 80 and 443), the implant C:\ProgramData\sync_agent.exe (PID 4412, running as CORP\svc_backup) calls ReadFile("customers_pii.csv"), slices each row into 48-byte chunks, hex-encodes the bytes (for example, turning "4102,john_smith,2065" into "343130322c6a6f686e5f736d6974682c32303635"), and calls DnsQuery_A(DNS_TYPE_TXT) to send a 112-byte UDP/53 DNS TXT query for 001.343130322c6a6f686e5f736d6974682c32303635.c2.badactor-dns.net to the Internal DNS Resolver (10.50.1.53:53). Standard DNS resolvers permit alphanumeric labels up to 63 characters per subdomain label. By hex-encoding 48-byte CSV chunks (producing a Shannon entropy of 4.48 bits/char compared to <3.2 for normal domain names) and querying the local corporate DNS resolver (10.50.1.53:53), sync_agent.exe (PID 4412) receives QueryStatus = 0 with QueryResults = "type: 16 ACK:001:NEXT;" (confirming chunk #001 was delivered and acknowledged so the loop can advance to chunk #002 after Sleep(150), while Sysmon Event ID 22 logs the query on the host). On the diagram, follow Step #1 / Link #1 (#1→ DNS TXT EXFIL / ⇠#1 ACK 112 B) from Node ③ (#3 Isolated Backup Host (DB-BACKUP-02)) to Node ④ (#4 sync_agent.exe (DNS Exfil Agent)), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Zeek DNS NDR & Sysmon EID 22).

stages.title: RECURSIVE RELAY THROUGH CORPORATE DNS SERVER
stages.subtitle: 100% cache miss forces recursive forwarding to attacker Name Server
stages.description: Because each postcard carries valid postage and a harmless street address, the postal clerk stamps them smoothly and sends them down the brass sorting chute. Here in Step 2 inside the post office, the intruder moves quietly past the postal scale & stamp window into neighboring restricted rooms without disturbing the registered certified mail safe. Because every single query from DB-BACKUP-02 contains a unique hex-encoded chunk of stolen data in the subdomain label (guaranteeing a 100% DNS cache miss rate so the resolver can never answer from local cache), the Internal DNS Resolver (10.50.1.53) follows standard recursive DNS resolution and forwards the 164-byte UDP/53 TXT query across the Egress Firewall directly to the authoritative Name Server for badactor-dns.net (ns1.badactor-dns.net at 45.133.1.99:53). While the Egress Firewall blocks direct outbound connections from DB-BACKUP-02 (10.50.1.12), it permits outbound UDP/53 recursive queries originating from the corporate DNS server (10.50.1.53, which receives back the authoritative TXT answer "ACK:001:NEXT" with TTL = 0.000000 and records the 164-byte exchange in Zeek dns.log). Mechanically, this stage is complete only after [object Object] and [object Object] is observed as live runtime state (the concrete checkpoint proving the previous stage's output now drives the next action). On the diagram, follow Step #2 / Link #2 (#2→ RECURSIVE TXT / ⇠#2 RESP 164 B) from Node ④ (#4 sync_agent.exe (DNS Exfil Agent)) to Node ② (#2 Corp DNS Resolver & FW), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Zeek DNS NDR & Sysmon EID 22).

stages.title: REASSEMBLE EXFILTRATED DATA & RETURN TXT C2 COMMAND
stages.subtitle: Bidirectional C2 payload returned inside DNS TXT response
stages.description: One harmless postcard at a time, an entire confidential binder is smuggled right out of the post office without ever raising the heavy parcel-inspection alarm. In this final step inside the post office, the intruder smuggles copied records out past the postal scale & stamp window in tiny disguised batches until the postmaster dispatch ledger catches the mismatch. When the recursive query arrives at the attacker’s authoritative Name Server (ns1.badactor-dns.net, 45.133.1.99:53), the dnscat2/exfil daemon strips the .c2.badactor-dns.net suffix, hex-decodes chunk #001 back into plaintext CSV rows (customers_pii.csv), and sends back a 188-byte DNS TXT response (TXT "ACK:001:CMD:SLEEP_60" with TTL = 0 seconds so the corporate DNS server will not cache the answer). The Internal DNS Resolver (10.50.1.53) relays that 188-byte TXT answer right back to sync_agent.exe (PID 4412) on DB-BACKUP-02 (10.50.1.12). This completes a bidirectional covert channel over UDP/53: outbound data exfiltration rides inside the DNS query subdomain labels (QNAME), while inbound acknowledgments and C2 tasking (the 188-byte TXT "ACK:001:CMD:SLEEP_60" response with rcode = 0 NOERROR and TTL = 0) ride back inside the DNS TXT answer record to pace the implant’s exfiltration loop. Mechanically, this stage is complete only after [object Object] and [object Object] is observed as live runtime state (the concrete checkpoint proving the previous stage's output now drives the next action). On the diagram, follow Step #3 / Link #3 (#3→ TXT C2 ACK & CMD / ⇠#3 RESP 188 B) from Node ② (#2 Corp DNS Resolver & FW) to Node ① (#1 Attacker Authoritative DNS C2), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Zeek DNS NDR & Sysmon EID 22).

detectionRule.title: High-Length Hex/Base64 Subdomain DNS Tunneling Detection
detectionRule.ruleCode:
title: Suspicious High-Length DNS Subdomain Query
logsource:
  product: windows
  category: dns_query
detection:
  selection:
    QueryName|re: '^[a-fA-F0-9]{24 }.'
  condition: selection
level: high
detectionRule.mitigation: Alert on high counts of unique subdomain queries per eTLD+1 in SIEM and block Newly Registered Domains (NRDs) via DNS RPZ.

detectionRule.title: DNS TXT Response Carrying Encoded C2 Tasking with Zero TTL
detectionRule.ruleCode:
title: Suspicious DNS TXT C2 Response with Zero TTL
logsource:
  category: dns
detection:
  selection:
    qtype_name: 'TXT'
    TTLs: '0.000000'
    answers|contains:
      - 'ACK:'
      - 'CMD:'
  condition: selection
level: critical
detectionRule.mitigation: Block authoritative resolution to newly registered domains (NRDs), strip or inspect high-entropy DNS TXT responses at the recursive resolver, and isolate DB-BACKUP-02 (10.50.1.12).
